PayPal AI Hackathon, 2026

GetPaid Agent

The problem

Freelancers and small merchants lose hours writing invoices and chasing late payments, time they could spend on the actual work.

Why I built it

For the PayPal AI Hackathon I wanted to test one idea: can an AI agent handle the boring parts of getting paid while a human stays fully in control of the money?

How it works

  1. You describe the invoice in one sentence.
  2. The AI turns it into a structured invoice draft and lists its assumptions. It is designed never to invent a client email or an amount.
  3. You review and approve. Nothing reaches PayPal without that click; the send endpoints refuse unapproved requests.
  4. The invoice goes out through the PayPal Invoicing API (sandbox).
  5. A live ledger tracks each invoice as awaiting, overdue or paid, refreshing every 15 seconds.
  6. For late invoices the agent drafts reminders whose tone matches how overdue they are, and you can edit them before sending.

Built carefully

Idempotency keys prevent duplicate invoices, every action goes into an audit trail, and AI calls are rate-limited per visitor.

Tools & tech

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Pydantic
  • Gemini LLM
  • PayPal Invoicing API
  • OAuth2
  • JavaScript
  • AG Grid
  • Render

Software engineering intern challenge

Lumen

The problem

AI chatbots often cite links they never opened, and they forget what you asked them yesterday.

Why I built it

The challenge was to build an agent with exactly one tool: web search. I focused on making it honest about where its answers come from, and on giving it a memory of earlier conversations.

How it works

  1. You ask a question; the agent decides how to search, with date filters shown above the answer.
  2. It searches the web through Tavily and reads the pages it gets back.
  3. The answer streams in live over Server-Sent Events.
  4. Sources are listed under the answer, and any link it didn't actually retrieve is removed.
  5. Each question is saved with its date, so a new chat can build on earlier ones, and the agent says when it does.
  6. If the main model hits its quota or slows down, a backup model takes over automatically.

Built carefully

56 automated tests that run without API keys, works with Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini, and a daily usage cap on the free Render deployment.

Tools & tech

  • TypeScript
  • Node.js
  • LLM agents
  • Tavily web search
  • Server-Sent Events
  • node:test
  • Render

Django web app, live on Render

MindCare

The problem

Students often miss the early signs of stress and low well-being, and many hesitate to talk about it or don't know where to start.

Why I built it

I wanted a responsible, privacy-first way for students to reflect on how they are doing: a confidential self-assessment that gives data-driven insight, without pretending to be a diagnosis.

How it works

  1. Register and log in, so every response stays private and confidential.
  2. Take a short, structured self-assessment about your emotional well-being.
  3. A machine learning model, trained on survey data, analyses the answers.
  4. You get predictive insights into your well-being patterns, clearly labelled as not a medical diagnosis.
  5. Clear guidance points you to professional help, and to emergency services if you ever feel unsafe.

Built carefully

Privacy-first by default, ethical by design with no clinical claims, and built to scale from one person to a whole institution.

Tools & tech

  • Python
  • Django
  • Machine learning
  • HTML
  • CSS
  • Render

Windows desktop app (SmartShot) · team project, I built most of it

Smart Screenshot Search Engine

The problem

Screenshots pile up with names like “Screenshot (231).png”. Finding the one that had a specific line of text means scrolling through hundreds of images.

Why I built it

I wanted to search my images by what's actually inside them, the words and the visuals, the same way I search text, without sending my files anywhere.

How it works

  1. Install it from a one-click Windows installer. No sign-up, no API key and no database setup: MongoDB is bundled and runs privately inside the app.
  2. Pick a folder, your Desktop or a whole drive. Every subfolder is scanned and junk like node_modules, .git and system folders is skipped.
  3. Tesseract OCR reads the text in every screenshot and photo, and text is pulled from PDFs and code files. After the first scan, only new or changed files are re-read.
  4. Search by keyword and filter by type, extension, size, date or whether text was found.
  5. Search by image: upload or crop one to find similar screenshots using perceptual hashing, and spot duplicate files.
  6. Ask about a file to get a summary, key points, dates, amounts or action items, all on your own computer. Save files and re-run past searches in one click.

Tools & tech

  • Electron
  • React
  • Node.js
  • Express
  • MongoDB
  • Tesseract OCR
  • Perceptual hashing
  • PyTorch (BLIP, CLIP)

Team research project, collaborator

ChemXAI

The problem

Neural networks can predict a molecule's properties well, but chemists can't trust a prediction they can't explain.

Why we built it

A research project on target-specific graph attention networks for molecular property prediction, with explainable AI that shows which atoms and bonds drive each prediction.

How it works

  1. Molecules from the QM9 dataset (about 131,000 of them) become graphs: atoms are nodes, bonds are edges.
  2. A graph attention network is trained for each target property: heat capacity, atomization enthalpy and atomization free energy.
  3. A saved 80/10/10 split makes every run reproducible, and explanations only use molecules the model never trained on.
  4. Each prediction is explained with attention weights, bond masking and Integrated Gradients.
  5. The bond rankings are checked against controls (random bonds and least-important bonds) to prove they mean something.
  6. A FastAPI backend serves training jobs, results and explanations to a React and TypeScript dashboard.

Built carefully

Nothing is faked: when a result or checkpoint doesn't exist yet, the app says so instead of showing a placeholder.

Tools & tech

  • Python
  • PyTorch
  • PyTorch Geometric
  • Graph neural networks
  • Explainable AI
  • FastAPI
  • React
  • TypeScript

Machine learning

Car Price Prediction

The problem

Used-car prices vary a lot, and buyers, sellers and dealers find it hard to know what a fair price is.

Why I built it

To see which factors really drive a car's resale value, and to turn that into a tool that gives a price estimate.

How it works

  1. Start from a real dataset of used-car listings from CarDekho.
  2. Explore how brand, year, mileage, fuel type and transmission affect price.
  3. Train regression models: Linear Regression, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting.
  4. Compare them on R², MAE and RMSE.
  5. Save the Random Forest model and use it in a small interface that predicts a price.

Tools & tech

  • Python
  • Machine learning
  • Random Forest
  • Regression
  • Jupyter
  • EDA

Data analytics

Pizza Sales Analysis

The problem

A restaurant needs to know what sells, in which size and at what time of day, to plan its stock and promotions.

Why I built it

To practise the full analyst workflow, from messy raw data to a dashboard a business owner could actually use.

How it works

  1. Clean and prepare four related tables (orders, order details, pizzas, pizza types) in Excel.
  2. Write 13 SQL queries for trends by pizza type, size, category, month, week and hour.
  3. Find the most and least popular pizzas; customer favourites include BBQ Chicken and Five Cheese.
  4. Build an interactive Power BI dashboard to tell the story visually.

Tools & tech

  • SQL
  • MySQL
  • Power BI
  • Excel
  • Data analytics
